newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel holds up, low sulphur quiet.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel holds up, low sulphur quiet.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices held up on Wednesday, continuing to ignore the weakness of crude and buoyed by a Portuguese tender award and Mediterranean activity, traders said.

A Scandinavian refiner sold around 12,000 tonnes of high sulphur in a combination cargo along with high sulphur VGO. The buyer was unidentified but paid $76 fob for the cracked fuel, in line with current prices.
High sulphur barges gained $2 in thin trade, with trades done at $85, $85.50 and $86. Bunker demand was moderate.
The announcement of the Portuguese state electricity company EdP's tender to buy up to 75,000 tonnes of high sulphur occupied much of the market's attention.
German trader Stinnes will supply one cargo while U.S. refiner and trading company Koch won the bid to supply two others, traders said. Delivery dates are April 21-25, April 26-30 and May 4-8.
The price was heard to be around $8 above the average of the north European and Mediterranean fob quotations.
Talk was pushing the Med market up as cargo deals were priced, traders said, and some of the enthusiasm drifted north.
Low sulphur markets were dead, drifting off $1 notionally to stay just under swaps levels.
But values were said to be unrealistic while no one is rushing to buy or sell and prices were seen coming under pressure from the chronic weakness in straight-run fuel values.
"All the cargoes are just sitting there but nothing is distressed yet," said one trader. "The bids are derisory and we've got a couple of weeks before things get desperate."
